shared_truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true. Every item below repeats this same rule so it reads standalone.

items.title: Before/After Transformation
items.when: The video's payoff is a visible change in one subject (a person, a room, a result) and the change itself is the hook.
items.composition: Split the frame into two halves showing the same subject in its before and after state - maximum visual contrast between the two states, same camera angle and framing on both sides so the comparison reads instantly.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Social UI (tweet / DM / review)
items.when: The video reacts to, replies to, or is triggered by a real message, comment, or review, and showing the message IS the information gap.
items.composition: A generic chat bubble, DM row, or star-review card placed beside the subject; a short truthful line of overlay text carries the message; never reproduce a real platform's brand marks or a real handle.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Three-Step Progression
items.when: The video tells a start-to-finish arc with a clear middle beat worth previewing (a challenge, a build, a transformation over time).
items.composition: Three vertical panels - start, mid story-beat, end - in one continuous frame or a plain split; an optional day/step badge on the last panel reinforces the arc.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Compelling Screenshot
items.when: The user has a real, striking frame from the source footage - not a generation task at all.
items.composition: Use the actual video frame as-is, or generate a Posed Action Shot that matches its first frame if no source clip is available. Flag to the user when they should supply the real frame instead of generating one.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Posed Portrait
items.when: The default framework whenever a specific person's presence and expression carry the hook and no stronger concept exists.
items.composition: The subject rendered large, filling most of the frame, with the identity lock and the lighting-rig blocks doing the work; very little or nothing in the background - the subject is the entire focus.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Posed Action Shot
items.when: The hook is a moment of action rather than a static expression - a stunt, a reaction, a physical event.
items.composition: One intriguing action caught mid-moment; keep the frame uncrowded with a single, unambiguous hero action.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Highlighting a Specific Day
items.when: The video covers a multi-day arc (a challenge, a build, a survival format) and one specific day is the most dramatic to preview.
items.composition: Any other framework, plus a large DAY N badge as overlay or baked text; pick a day from the last fifth of the arc so it reads as a climax, not a midpoint.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Graphical Representation
items.when: The hook is a data point, comparison, or idea better shown as a diagram than as a photoreal scene.
items.composition: A clean, non-photoreal diagram or graphic brief (a curve, a simple familiar chart shape) in place of the photoreal frame block; drop the lighting-rig language entirely for this framework.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Landscape
items.when: The location or environment itself is the draw - a place, a scale of nature, a striking setting.
items.composition: The environment is the hero of the frame; keep one small subject placed on a power third for scale and human interest; the lighting rig is optional here.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Map / Aerial
items.when: The video is about a journey, a route, or a geographic comparison.
items.composition: A map or an aerial photo as the frame; a highlighted route or point (a circle, an arrow, a short truthful label) supplies the information gap.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Product
items.when: The video's answer is a specific product and showing it is the payoff, not a spoiler.
items.composition: The product is the sharp, hero subject of the frame; open the gap by making the product itself the answer to the title's implied question rather than explaining it.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Adding Text
items.when: A short word or phrase sharpens a concept that is otherwise visually complete.
items.composition: Use the overlay-preset text stack by default, or baked text only on explicit request; treat the text as a callout (an arrow plus one word) or as the continuation of the title's question, never as a caption that restates the image.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Repetition of Objects
items.when: The hook is quantity or excess - a large amount of one thing is inherently surprising.
items.composition: A large quantity of one object filling the frame while staying individually legible; add one context element and a subject for scale.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Size Difference
items.when: The hook is an extreme scale contrast central to the story - giant versus tiny, one versus a crowd.
items.composition: Extreme scale contrast between two elements central to the story, staged in the same frame so the comparison is immediate.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: News Clip
items.when: The video frames itself as breaking, urgent, or newsworthy and that urgency is the hook.
items.composition: A generic breaking-news lower-third or chyron over the image, generic broadcaster styling, one short truthful line; never reproduce a real network's brand marks.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.

items.title: Amplified Reality
items.when: A real element from the story is already striking and exaggerating it further sharpens the hook without inventing anything.
items.composition: Build on a Posed Action Shot and exaggerate exactly one real element from the story (make it oversized or more intense); keep it plausible - over-amplification kills trust.
items.truth_rule: The image may exaggerate but must honestly represent the video. A concept that misrepresents the content breaks viewer trust - keep any baked or overlay text short and true.
